title: indigo_mount_lx200: generic, classic and stargo2 profiles report a false slew right after connect
description: Found in the review of d0a643e1. For profiles whose poll decodes the motion state with meade_update_generic_state() (generic, classic, stargo2) the first poll after connect compares the coordinates just read with PRIVATE_DATA->lastRA/lastDec, which are 0 in freshly allocated private data and are set only at the end of each poll (indigo_mount_lx200.driver:3497, :3735-3736). Unless the mount happens to point within 2' of RA 0 / Dec 0 the first poll therefore sees a 'slew': MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES and the slew light go BUSY for one poll period (measured on the simulator: OK -> BUSY at ~0.1 s -> OK at ~0.7 s after connect). Visible effects: a client sees a slew that does not exist, and since d0a643e1 a MOUNT_ON_COORDINATES_SET change or coordinates request in that window is refused with ALERT. Expected: the first poll of a connection seeds lastRA/lastDec from its own reading (and the values are reset at disconnect/connect so a reconnect at another position behaves the same) and reports no motion; a real slew detected by later polls is unchanged. Scope: indigo_mount_lx200.driver (version bump, regenerate), a simulator-backed case per affected profile proving the coordinates never go BUSY after connect, and removal of nothing in test_mount_lx200_simulator.c that other cases need (lx_select_mode retry may stay). Recorded run with tools/run_driver_test.py mount_lx200; MIGRATION_STATUS count.
